forms: name the place of a digit
which digit is in a named place
how many places a number has
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PLACE_VALUE.mastery: Given a whole number up to 999,999,999 the child names the place of any digit (ones to hundred millions), including digits beside zeros, and says which digit sits in a named place. Numbers come from real settings such as a county budget or the number of phone lines.

forms: total value of an underlined digit
total values of two digits added
difference between two digits of the same value
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.TOTAL_VALUE.mastery: Given a whole number up to 999,999,999 the child gives the total value of a chosen digit (digit times its place), adds the total values of two digits, and writes the number in expanded form. The child does not mistake a digit for its total value.

forms: read a number aloud in groups
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SYMBOLS_HM.mastery: Given a number said or written in parts (for example 45 million, 12 thousand and 7) the child writes it in figures with every place filled and zero as a place holder, and reads a figure aloud in groups of three. Numbers up to 999,999,999.

forms: choose the words for a figure
write a cheque amount in words
spot the mistake in the words
say the same number two ways
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.WORDS_FROM_.mastery: The child writes a number up to 9,999,999 in words with British spelling, a hyphen in twenty-one to ninety-nine, and each group (millions, thousands, hundreds) in order. Zeros in a group are not spoken. The design limit for words is millions.

forms: order two numbers given in words
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.FIGURES_FRO.mastery: Given a number in words up to millions, such as "two million and forty-five thousand and seven", the child writes it in figures with zero place holders in every empty place.

forms: round the same number two ways
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ROUND_TO_PL.mastery: The child rounds a number up to 999,999,999 to the nearest ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, hundred thousand, million, ten million or hundred million: looks at the digit just to the right, rounds up on 5 or more, and writes zeros in all places after the one rounded.

forms: round the number in a report
why a rounded number is not exact
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ROUND_IN_CO.mastery: Given a real setting (a population, a county budget, a news report) the child chooses the sensible place to round to, rounds the number, and says why the rounded number is only an estimate. Rounding a carried digit (such as 999,500 to the nearest thousand) is included.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.EVEN_ODD.mastery: The child classifies any whole number up to millions as even or odd by its last digit, and knows that sums and products of even and odd numbers follow a pattern (even + even is even, odd + odd is even, even x anything is even).

forms: pick the primes from a table
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PRIME_NUMBE.mastery: The child tells prime from composite numbers up to 100 by testing small divisors, knows that 1 is neither, that 2 is the only even prime, and that an odd number is not always prime. The child lists the primes up to 50.

forms: sum or difference in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ADD_SUB_LAR.mastery: The child adds and subtracts whole numbers of up to nine digits in a column, regrouping across zeros, and decides whether to add or subtract in a story about money, population or distance. Answers are checked by estimating.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.MULT_LARGE.mastery: The child multiplies a number of up to 4 digits by a number of up to 3 digits using long multiplication, with the zero place holder in the second and third rows, and by 10, 100 and 1,000 by shifting the digits. The product is checked by estimating.

forms: what the remainder means in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.DIV_LARGE.mastery: The child divides a number of up to 6 digits by a number of up to 3 digits by long division, with zeros in the quotient where a digit does not fit, writes the remainder as a whole number, and checks by multiplying back.

forms: put in brackets to make a value
find the mistake in the order
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ORDER_OF_OP.mastery: The child works out expressions of up to three operations with brackets, working brackets first, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. Numbers up to 3 digits.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.OPERATIONS_.mastery: The child reads a story with two or three steps (fares, fuel, rent, bags and rows), chooses the operations, works them in order and writes the answer with its unit. Money left, total takings and equal sharing are included.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SEQ_EXTEND_.mastery: Given the first four to six terms of a sequence with a constant difference or a constant multiplier, the child finds the rule, continues the sequence, and spots a term that does not fit.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SEQ_NTH_TER.mastery: For a sequence that goes up or down by the same amount, the child finds a distant term (for example the 12th) by first term plus the number of steps times the difference, and does not count the first term as a step.

forms: write the terms from a rule
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SEQ_CREATE_.mastery: Given a rule such as "start at 5, add 4" or "multiply by 3 then add 3", the child writes the first terms, and makes a sequence of their own for a number game, checking that the terms follow the rule every time.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.DIV_BY_2_4_8_5_10.mastery: The child tests a number up to 6 digits for divisibility by 2, 5 and 10 from the last digit, by 4 from the last two digits and by 8 from the last three digits, and explains the test.

forms: divisible by 6: count from a table
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.DIV_BY_3_6_9.mastery: The child adds the digits of a number up to 6 digits and tests the sum for 3 and 9, and knows a number is divisible by 6 only when it is even and divisible by 3.

forms: spot the slip in the working
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.DIV_BY_11.mastery: The child adds the digits in the odd places and in the even places, subtracts the two sums, and says the number is divisible by 11 when the difference is 0 or a multiple of 11.

forms: find the mistake in the working
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.PRIME_FACTORISE.mastery: The child splits a number up to 500 with a factor tree or repeated division by 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 until every factor is prime, writes repeated factors in full or with a power, and explains why a number with no small factors may still be composite.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.GCD_BY_FACTORS.mastery: The child writes each of two or three numbers (up to 200) as a product of primes, multiplies the primes common to all of them, taking each as many times as it is in every number, and gets the GCD.

forms: why the product is not the least
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.LCM_BY_FACTORS.mastery: The child writes each of two or three numbers (up to 60) as a product of primes and multiplies each prime the greatest number of times it appears in any one number, and gets the LCM.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.GCD_IN_CONTEXT.mastery: The child decides from a story that the greatest equal size or number of equal groups is the GCD (cutting ropes, packing boxes, tiling) and works it out for two or three quantities, answering the size or the number asked.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.LCM_IN_CONTEXT.mastery: The child decides from a story that the first time two or three repeating events coincide is the LCM (matatus leaving, bells ringing) and works it out in minutes or days, answering the time asked.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.COMPARE_FRACTIO.mastery: The child compares two or three fractions with denominators up to 12 by renaming them with a common denominator, decides which is greater, orders them, and can explain why a bigger denominator does not mean a bigger fraction.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.ADD_UNLIKE_FRAC.mastery: The child adds two fractions or mixed numbers with unlike denominators (up to 12) by renaming with the LCM, adds numerators, carries any whole from the fraction part, and writes the sum in simplest form.

forms: what is left in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.SUBTRACT_UNLIKE.mastery: The child subtracts fractions or mixed numbers with unlike denominators (up to 12) by renaming with the LCM, regroups a whole into the fraction part when needed, reduces the whole by one, and simplifies.

forms: multiply a fraction by a whole number
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.MULT_FRACTION_B.mastery: The child multiplies a fraction by a whole number (and finds a fraction of a quantity), multiplying the numerator and keeping the denominator, simplifies, and writes an improper result as a mixed number.

The child multiplies a fraction by a fraction or a mixed number by writing mixed numbers as improper fractions, multiplying numerators and denominators, simplifying (also across before multiplying), and finds a fraction of a fraction of an amount in a story.

forms: use a reciprocal in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.RECIPROCAL.mastery: The child writes the reciprocal by turning a fraction upside down, writes a whole number as a fraction over 1 first, writes a mixed number as an improper fraction first, and checks that the number times its reciprocal is 1.

forms: divide a fraction by a whole number
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.DIVIDE_FRACTION.mastery: The child divides a fraction or a mixed number by a whole number by multiplying the denominator (or by the reciprocal), simplifies, and knows the result is smaller than the fraction.

forms: divide a fraction by a fraction
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.DIVIDE_BY_FRACT.mastery: The child divides a whole number, fraction or mixed number by a fraction or a mixed number by multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor (the second number only), writing mixed numbers as improper fractions first.

forms: divide a whole number by a fraction
will the answer be larger or smaller
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.DIVIDE_WHOLE_BY.mastery: The child divides a whole number by a fraction, chooses division when the story asks how many small amounts fit into a large one (cups from a jug, bags from a sack), and knows the answer is larger than the whole number.

forms: a whole number as a term
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_SEQ_AD.mastery: The child finds the constant gap between terms of a sequence of fractions with a common denominator, keeps the denominator, and writes the next terms and a term that is a whole number as a fraction.

forms: spot the term that does not fit
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_SEQ_MU.mastery: The child finds that terms such as 1, 1/3, 1/9 follow a constant ratio, states the rule (divide by 3, or multiply by 1/3), and continues the sequence.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_SEQ_IN.mastery: Given a table of the part of a task done after equal times (2, 4, 6 hours), the child finds the part done per step, and answers when the task is complete or how much is done at a later time, counting hours and not steps.

forms: write the first terms from a rule
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_SEQ_CR.mastery: The child writes a sequence of fractions from a rule (add 1/4, or multiply by 1/2), keeps every term in line with the rule, and writes a rule for a puzzle sequence of their own that a partner can solve.

forms: write the number from a chart
which digit is in the place
MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DEC_PLACE_AND_TO.mastery: The child names the place of a digit after the point (tenths, hundredths, thousandths), gives its total value (the 7 in 4.073 is worth 0.07), and writes a decimal from a place value chart whose rows are not in order.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DEC_COUNT_TENTHS.mastery: The child says how many tenths (or hundredths) make a decimal such as 7.7 (77 tenths) by counting the whole ones as ten tenths each.

forms: find the mistake with the point
MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.MULT_DEC_BY_WHOL.mastery: The child multiplies a decimal with up to three places by a whole number up to 100 by multiplying without the point and putting the point back with the same number of places, and decides if the answer is sensible.

forms: is the product bigger or smaller
MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.MULT_DEC_BY_DEC.mastery: The child multiplies two decimals by multiplying without points and giving the product as many decimal places as both factors together, uses it for the area of a rectangle with decimal sides, and says when the product is smaller than a factor.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DIV_DEC_BY_WHOLE.mastery: The child divides a decimal by a whole number, and a whole number by a whole number with a decimal quotient (12 / 8 = 1.5), by long division with the point in the quotient directly above the point in the dividend.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DIV_BY_DECIMAL.mastery: The child divides by a decimal by moving the point in both numbers the same number of places until the divisor is whole, uses it to count how many small amounts fit into a large one, and finds a price per kilogram.

forms: why is the answer bigger than 6
MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DEC_DIVISION_SIZ.mastery: The child says that dividing by a number less than 1 makes the answer larger and dividing by a number greater than 1 makes it smaller, using how many lots fit, and does not move the point without a reason.

forms: square of a multiple of ten
MATH.G7.NUMBER.SQUARES_AND_SQUARE_ROOTS..mastery: The child finds the square of a whole number up to 50, and of multiples of 10 (30 squared is 900), by multiplying the number by itself, and knows that squaring is not doubling.
The child squares a fraction by multiplying the numerator by itself and the denominator by itself, simplifies, and says why the answer is smaller than the fraction.

The child squares a decimal such as 0.03 or 1.5 by multiplying without the point and giving the square twice as many decimal places, and uses it for the area of a square plot and for the area when the side is doubled.
The child finds the square root of a perfect square up to 2,500 by finding the number that multiplied by itself gives it, checks by squaring, and knows the root of a sum is not the sum of the roots.

The child finds the root of a fraction by taking the root of the numerator and of the denominator (9/16 gives 3/4), and of a decimal that is a perfect square (0.09 gives 0.3 and 1.44 gives 1.2) by halving the decimal places.
The child takes the square root of the area of a square plot to find a side, then uses the side (for the distance round, or to compare plots), reading the question to know which is needed.

forms: which perfect squares are either side
MATH.G7.NUMBER.SQUARES_AND_SQUARE_ROOTS..mastery: The child finds the two perfect squares either side of a number (98 lies between 81 and 100) and so places its root between two whole numbers (between 9 and 10). The number is not itself a perfect square: this skill supports checking roots.

forms: choose the expression from a table
write the charge for n items
MATH.G7.ALGEBR.ALGEBRAIC_EXPRESSIONS.FOR.mastery: From a table or story (delivery of n jerricans at sh 30 each plus sh 10), the child writes the expression rate x n + fixed, tests it with n = 1 and n = 2, and says what each part means.

Given one person is x years old, another is 2 years younger and another is 3 times as old, the child writes an expression for each and for their total, using brackets only when a whole group is taken.

forms: less than in the right order
MATH.G7.ALGEBR.ALGEBRAIC_EXPRESSIONS.FOR.mastery: The child turns words such as "3 more than x", "5 less than n", "twice y and then 4 more" and "a third of m" into expressions, keeping the order for "less than".

forms: find a and b in ax + b
MATH.G7.ALGEBR.ALGEBRAIC_EXPRESSIONS.SIM.mastery: The child collects the x terms and the number terms of an expression with up to three terms of each kind, keeps each sign, counts a plain x as 1x, and substitutes a value to check or to use.
The child multiplies every term inside a bracket by the number outside, collects like terms, and does not join an x term with a number term.

MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_EQUATIONS.FORM_EQU.mastery: From a story with a price for each item, a fixed amount and a total (8 books and a geometry set, total sh 398) the child writes an equation such as 8x + 150 = 398, with the fixed amount added once and on the same side as the books.

forms: solve from a table of values
MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_EQUATIONS.SOLVE_TW.mastery: The child solves equations like 6x + 6 = 78 and 3n + 3 = 45 by undoing the added or subtracted number first and then the multiplier, doing the same to both sides, and checks by putting the answer back.

forms: solve with x on both sides
MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_EQUATIONS.SOLVE_BO.mastery: The child solves equations like 4x - 4 = 2x + 12 by taking the smaller x term from both sides, then undoing the number, then dividing, and checks in both sides.

MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_EQUATIONS.EQUATION.mastery: The child explains that an equation is a balance, so what is done to one side must be done to the other, and that the unknown can be on either side.

MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_EQUATIONS.SOLVE_IN.mastery: The child forms an equation for a story (ages after some years, a parking charge with a fixed part, equal boxes and loose items, money left after spending), solves it, and answers the quantity the question asks for, not the unknown.

forms: is the statement true for this value
MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_INEQUALITIES.INEQU.mastery: The child picks <, >, <= or >= for "at least", "at most", "fewer than", "no more than", "not less than" and "under", says whether the number itself is allowed, and tests a statement such as a <= 12 by putting in a value.

MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_INEQUALITIES.FORM_.mastery: From a limit in a story (a pick-up that carries at most 1,000 kg with 200 kg already on it, a hall with seats left) the child writes an inequality such as 200 + 50n <= 1,000, with the amount already there included and the sign that fits the limit.

MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_INEQUALITIES.SOLVE.mastery: The child forms bag + books <= money, takes away the fixed cost, divides by the price, and gives the greatest whole number of items that fits (8.75 gives 8, not 9), checking that one more would cost too much.

forms: which number is in the shading
MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_INEQUALITIES.SIMPL.mastery: The child puts a closed circle for <= or >= and an open circle for < or > at the number in the inequality, shades towards the bigger numbers for > and >= and the smaller ones for < and <=, and reads which numbers lie under the shading.

MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_INEQUALITIES.FORM_.mastery: The child writes a range with two ends, such as 6 <= a < 12, choosing the sign at each end from the words, lists the whole numbers that fit, tests a value against both ends, and writes "less than 2 or greater than 7" as two separate inequalities, never as 7 < x < 2.

MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_INEQUALITIES.SOLVE.mastery: The child solves 8 < 2x + 4 <= 20 by taking 4 from all three parts and dividing all three by 2, gets 2 < x <= 8, and lists the whole numbers 3 to 8 that fit, leaving out an end the sign leaves out.

forms: which inequality does the line show
MATH.G7.ALGEBR.LINEAR_INEQUALITIES.COMPO.mastery: The child reads two circles and the shading between them as a compound inequality, with the smaller number on the left, <= at a closed circle and < at an open one, and draws such a line from an inequality.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.PYTHAGOREAN_RELATIONSHIP..mastery: The child finds the right angle in a triangle labelled with letters, names the hypotenuse as the side opposite the right angle (and the longest side), and names the other two sides as the legs.

forms: why does 5, 12, 13 show a right angle
find the mistake in the test
MATH.G7.MEASUR.PYTHAGOREAN_RELATIONSHIP..mastery: The child squares the two shorter sides, adds them, and compares with the square of the longest side (exactly equal means a right angle), and explains why a 3, 4, 5 or 5, 12, 13 corner is square.
The child squares the two shorter sides, adds them and takes the square root to find the hypotenuse, and uses it for a brace on a gate, a wire from a pole to a peg and a diagonal path.
The child subtracts the square of the known shorter side from the square of the hypotenuse and takes the square root, and knows a square root is not halving.
The child finds the straight path as the hypotenuse, adds the two sides for the long way, and subtracts to find how much shorter the straight path is, answering the quantity the question asks for.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.LENGTH.CONVERT_LENGTH_UNI.mastery: The child changes a length between cm, dm, m, Dm and Hm by multiplying when going to a smaller unit and dividing when going to a bigger one, using the number of small units in one big unit (1 m = 10 dm = 100 cm; 1 Hm = 100 m), also in two stages.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.LENGTH.COMPARE_LENGTHS_UN.mastery: The child reads the size of each unit from a table, changes both lengths to the same unit, and finds how much longer one is, answering in the unit asked.

forms: which unit is the answer in
MATH.G7.MEASUR.LENGTH.OPERATIONS_ON_LENG.mastery: The child works with lengths in a story (rope cut into pieces, posts along a fence): changes to one unit, finds the total of several pieces, subtracts what is left, and counts posts on a straight fence as gaps plus one.

forms: which plot needs the longest fence
MATH.G7.MEASUR.LENGTH.PERIMETER_PLANE_FI.mastery: The child finds the distance round a rectangle as 2 x (length + width), round an L-shape by adding every edge, compares plots by perimeter and not by area, and counts posts round a closed plot as distance divided by gap.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.LENGTH.CIRCUMFERENCE_DIST.mastery: The child finds the circumference as pi x diameter (22/7 or 3.14 as the question says), uses it for the distance a wheel travels in many turns (changing cm to m), and for a track made of straight sides and half circles.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.LENGTH.CIRCUMFERENCE_FIND.mastery: Given the distance round a circle, the child divides by pi (multiplies by 7/22) to find the diameter, halves it for the radius, and checks by multiplying back.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.LENGTH.CIRCUMFERENCE_REAS.mastery: The child says the circumference is always about 3.14 times the diameter, so doubling the diameter doubles the circumference, and finds the pattern in a table of measured circles.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_M2_CM2.mastery: The child says a square metre is a square 100 cm by 100 cm, so 1 m2 = 10,000 cm2, changes m2 to cm2 by multiplying by 10,000 and cm2 to m2 by dividing, and finds the wrong step in a working that uses 100.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.AREA.LAND_UNITS_HA_ACRE.mastery: The child says 1 hectare is 10,000 m2 (a square 100 m by 100 m), finds a field in hectares from its length and width, totals plots in m2 and changes to hectares, and uses the acre size the question gives to change acres to m2.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_PARALLELOGRAM_R.mastery: The child multiplies the base by the perpendicular height, not the slanting side, explains that cutting a triangle off one end and moving it makes a rectangle, and finds a rhombus from base x height or half the product of its diagonals.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_TRAPEZIUM.mastery: The child adds the two parallel sides, multiplies by the distance between them and halves, finds a missing parallel side by doubling the area, dividing by the height and taking away the known side, and spots a working that doubles instead of halving.

forms: how many cover the whole floor
MATH.G7.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_RECT_IN_CONTEXT.mastery: The child puts the floor and one tile in the same unit (cm2), divides the floor area by the area of one tile, and does not count tiles along the edges only.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_CIRCLE.mastery: The child halves the diameter for the radius, multiplies pi x r x r with pi = 22/7, halves for a half circle, and explains that doubling the radius makes the area four times as big.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_CIRCLE_FROM_CIR.mastery: From the circumference the child finds the diameter (divide by pi), halves it for the radius, then finds pi x r x r, keeping each step in order.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_BORDERS.mastery: The child finds the outer shape (a rectangle grows by twice the path width each way; a circle grows by the path width on its radius), finds the inner shape, and takes the inner area from the outer area.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_COMBINED_SHAPES.mastery: The child splits an L-shaped floor or a stage into rectangles and a half circle, finds each area, adds them, and multiplies the whole area by the cost of one square metre.

forms: blocks that make a cubic metre
MATH.G7.MEASUR.VOLUME_AND_CAPACITY.CUBIC.mastery: The child says a cubic metre is a cube 100 cm by 100 cm by 100 cm (1,000,000 cm3), changes m3 to cm3 and back, and says why the three lengths are multiplied and not added.

forms: volume of a cube from its wire
how many cubes pack a carton
MATH.G7.MEASUR.VOLUME_AND_CAPACITY.VOLUM.mastery: The child finds the volume of a cuboid or cube from its edges, finds the edge of a cube from the total length of its wire (12 edges), counts blocks that pack a carton exactly, and finds a missing height by dividing the volume by the base area.
The child finds the radius from the diameter, the base area (pi x radius x radius), multiplies by the height for the volume, and works backwards to a height from the volume, and to litres.

forms: one litre is how many cm3
MATH.G7.MEASUR.VOLUME_AND_CAPACITY.VOLUM.mastery: The child changes m3 to litres (x 1,000) and cm3 to litres (divide by 1,000), and states the relation between cm3, ml and litres.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.VOLUME_AND_CAPACITY.CAPAC.mastery: The child changes the quantity and the container to the same unit, then divides to find how many jerricans fill a tank, how many cups come from a can, or how many days a tank lasts from the total daily use.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.TIME_DISTANCE_AND_SPEED.T.mastery: The child changes seconds to minutes and hours (60 and 3,600) and back, writes a time such as 8,400 seconds as hours and minutes (2 h 20 min), and never treats an hour as 100 minutes.
The child reads a timetable on the 24-hour clock, finds the time of each leg, leaves out the waiting time at a stop, and gives the moving time in minutes.

forms: to and from school for a week
MATH.G7.MEASUR.TIME_DISTANCE_AND_SPEED.D.mastery: The child changes metres to kilometres (divide by 1,000) and back, finds a total distance such as laps or a return trip over several days, and answers in the unit asked.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.TIME_DISTANCE_AND_SPEED.S.mastery: The child changes the time to hours (75 min is 1.25 h, with minutes out of 60), divides the distance by it, and does not multiply or invert; a timetable gives the time between two 24-hour readings.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.TIME_DISTANCE_AND_SPEED.T.mastery: The child finds time as distance divided by speed, and changes a decimal number of hours to minutes by multiplying the decimal part by 60 (2.5 h = 150 min).

MATH.G7.MEASUR.TIME_DISTANCE_AND_SPEED.A.mastery: The child finds the time of each part (distance divided by speed), adds them, and divides the total distance by the total time; the slower part takes longer, so the average is not halfway between the speeds.

forms: find speed in m/s from metres and seconds
MATH.G7.MEASUR.TIME_DISTANCE_AND_SPEED.S.mastery: The child changes km/h to m/s by multiplying by 1,000 and dividing by 3,600 (divide by 3.6), and m/s to km/h by multiplying by 3.6, and explains why an hour has 3,600 seconds.
The child changes all speeds to km/h (or all to m/s) before saying which is fastest, and does not compare a number in m/s with a number in km/h.

forms: a reading for a hot day
MATH.G7.MEASUR.TEMPERATURE.TEMP_WORDS.mastery: The child reads a table of temperature ranges and says whether a reading in degrees Celsius is cold, cool, warm or hot, and gives a sensible temperature for a day described in words.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.TEMPERATURE.TEMP_COMPARE_.mastery: The child says which of two places is hotter, warmer or colder, finds the difference between two readings (counting through zero when one is below it), and the difference between the highest and lowest points of a graph.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.TEMPERATURE.TEMP_UNITS.mastery: The child names degree Celsius and kelvin as units, knows water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius (273 K) and boils at 100 degrees Celsius (373 K), writes kelvin without a degree sign, and knows a Kelvin reading is larger than the Celsius reading.

forms: a fall of temperature in kelvin
MATH.G7.MEASUR.TEMPERATURE.TEMP_CONVERT_.mastery: The child adds 273 to change degrees Celsius to kelvin and subtracts 273 for the reverse, knows a change in temperature is the same in both units, and puts both on one scale before comparing.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.TEMPERATURE.TEMP_RISES_FA.mastery: The child starts from the first reading, adds each rise and subtracts each fall in turn, and gives the final temperature in degrees Celsius or kelvin.

forms: selling price from cost and profit
MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.PROFIT_AND_LOSS.mastery: The child finds profit as selling money minus cost and loss as cost minus selling money, for one item or for many (kilograms of tomatoes), and says which it is.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.PROFIT_WITH_EXTRA_C.mastery: The child adds extra costs (delivery, transport) to the cost of the goods, finds the money from selling all the items, and takes the total cost from it.

forms: which item gave the best percentage
MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.PERCENT_PROFIT_LOSS.mastery: The child finds the profit or loss in shillings, divides it by the buying price (not the selling price) and multiplies by 100, and compares items by percentage, not by the shilling amount.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.DISCOUNT_AND_PERCEN.mastery: The child finds a discount as marked price minus price paid, writes it as a percentage of the marked price, takes a percentage discount off the marked price, and explains that a second discount is taken off the new, smaller price.

forms: check by taking the discount off
MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.DISCOUNT_WORK_BACK.mastery: The child says that after a 20% discount the price paid is 80% of the marked price, finds 1% and then 100%, and does not add 20% of the price paid back on.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.COMMISSION.mastery: The child changes the rate to a decimal by dividing by 100, works out commission on the right part of the sales (all, or only the part above a target), and adds the basic salary for the month's pay.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.INTERPRET_UTILITY_B.mastery: The child finds the units used as the difference of two meter readings, charges each band of units at its own rate, adds the fixed charge, and finds the units a token buys after the charges are taken.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.INTERPRET_SHOP_BILL.mastery: The child multiplies each line by the number bought, adds the lines for the total, and takes the total from the note given for the change.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.PREPARE_BILL.mastery: The child writes each item with its quantity, unit price and line total, matches units (a price per kg with a mass in kg), adds all the lines and states the total to pay.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.POSTAL_CHARGES.mastery: The child finds the band for each parcel by its own mass, adds the charge for each parcel posted, and for a rate such as sh 80 for the first 100 g and sh 30 for each extra 100 g counts one fewer extra part.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.MOBILE_MONEY_SERVIC.mastery: The child names the service for a task: send money to a person, withdraw cash at an agent, deposit cash, pay a school fee to a paybill with an account number, pay a shop through a till (buy goods), buy airtime, save or borrow, and says which ones carry a charge.

MATH.G7.MEASUR.MONEY.MOBILE_MONEY_TRANSA.mastery: The child finds the charge for each send or withdrawal from its own row of a table, adds the charges for separate transactions, and finds the balance left after the amount and the charge both leave the account.

MATH.G7.GEOMET.ANGLES.ANGLES_ON_LINE.mastery: The child uses the fact that angles side by side on a straight line add to 180 degrees, finds a missing angle, and with angles such as (3x + 10) and (2x + 20) forms 5x + 30 = 180, solves for x and puts it back to find each angle.

MATH.G7.GEOMET.ANGLES.VERTICALLY_OPPOSIT.mastery: The child says that where two straight lines cross the opposite angles are equal and the angles beside each other add to 180, and finds all four angles from one.

forms: angles in x at a point
MATH.G7.GEOMET.ANGLES.ANGLES_AT_POINT.mastery: The child uses the fact that the angles round a point make a full turn of 360 degrees and finds a missing angle by taking all the known angles from 360.

MATH.G7.GEOMET.ANGLES.TRANSVERSAL_ANGLE_.mastery: The child names alternate, corresponding and co-interior angles from where they sit, says that alternate and corresponding angles are equal and co-interior angles add to 180, finds each angle, and gives the reason.

forms: angle next to a given angle
MATH.G7.GEOMET.ANGLES.PARALLELOGRAM_ANGL.mastery: The child says opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal and neighbouring angles add to 180 (they are co-interior), finds all four angles from one, and in a rhombus uses the isosceles triangle a diagonal makes.

forms: base angles of an isosceles roof
MATH.G7.GEOMET.ANGLES.TRIANGLE_ANGLE_PRO.mastery: The child uses the angle sum of 180, the equal base angles of an isosceles triangle, and the exterior angle that equals the two far interior angles, and solves a triangle whose angles are written in x.

MATH.G7.GEOMET.ANGLES.POLYGON_ANGLE_SUM.mastery: The child splits a polygon from one corner into triangles, two fewer than the sides, says why any quadrilateral adds to 360, and finds the angle sum (n - 2) x 180 or the number of sides from a sum.

forms: why 360 divided by n is the exterior
MATH.G7.GEOMET.ANGLES.INTERIOR_EXTERIOR_.mastery: The child says the exterior angles of a polygon make one full turn (360), that an interior and exterior angle at a corner add to 180, and that 360 divided by the sides of a regular polygon gives its exterior angle, not its interior one.

forms: each angle of a regular hexagon
MATH.G7.GEOMET.ANGLES.REGULAR_POLYGON_SO.mastery: The child finds each interior angle of a regular pentagon or hexagon from the angle sum, finds the number of sides from an exterior or interior angle, and spots a working that splits a polygon into the wrong number of triangles.

MATH.G7.GEOMET.GEOMETRICAL_CONSTRUCTION..mastery: The child places the centre of the protractor on the corner and the base line along one arm, reads the scale that starts at zero on that arm, and states whether the angle is acute, right, obtuse or reflex.

The child bisects an angle with a ruler and compasses (arc across both arms from the corner, two equal arcs from those marks, line through the crossing point), says each half is half the original, and gives the reason for each arc.

forms: find the mistake in the plan
MATH.G7.GEOMET.GEOMETRICAL_CONSTRUCTION..mastery: The child plans which angles to construct and how often to bisect to get 90, 60, 45, 30, 15 and 7.5 degrees, and builds angles such as 135 or 105 by adding or subtracting these.

forms: why the arcs do not meet
MATH.G7.GEOMET.GEOMETRICAL_CONSTRUCTION..mastery: The child decides whether three side lengths make a triangle (the two shorter sides together must be longer than the longest), and plans the construction of a triangle from its sides or from two sides and the angle between them.

forms: draw a circle of diameter 6 cm
MATH.G7.GEOMET.GEOMETRICAL_CONSTRUCTION..mastery: The child sets the compasses to the radius (half the diameter), places the point at the centre, and draws a circle, and says that every point on it is the same distance from the centre.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.DATA_MEANIN.mastery: The child says data is facts or numbers collected to answer a question (the fruit learners choose is data, as well as their heights), plans a question whose answers can be counted, and records each answer once, for example with a tally.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.FREQUENCY_T.mastery: The child counts tallies in fives (a gate of four strokes and one across is 5), writes each frequency, finds a missing frequency from the total, and reads the most common value from the row with the biggest frequency.
The child multiplies each value by its frequency and adds to find a total (goals, books), adds the rows a question asks about, and writes that count as a percentage of the total frequency.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.GRAPH_SCALE.mastery: The child divides the largest value by each scale to see how many squares the tallest bar needs, picks the smallest scale that still fits the axis, and for a pictograph picks a symbol value that shows every number with whole and half symbols and keeps the longest row short enough.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.PICTOGRAPH.mastery: The child counts whole and half symbols in a row, multiplies by what one symbol stands for, and answers "how many more" by the difference of two rows.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.BAR_GRAPH_D.mastery: The child labels both axes, numbers the vertical axis in equal steps from 0, draws bars of equal width with equal gaps, and makes each bar the height of its value.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.BAR_GRAPH_I.mastery: The child reads each bar against the scale, picks out the bars a question asks about (the two busiest days, the highest and the lowest), and adds or subtracts them as the question asks.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.CHOOSE_GRAP.mastery: The child says a bar graph compares separate groups, a line graph shows one measurement changing over time, and a pie chart shows how one whole is shared into parts, and matches the data to the graph.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.PIE_CHART_D.mastery: The child says the sectors of a pie chart make a full turn of 360 degrees, finds a missing angle by taking the others from 360, and works an angle out from a count (count / total x 360) and back.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.PIE_CHART_I.mastery: The child turns a sector angle into a percentage (angle / 360 x 100) or a count (angle / 360 x total), and explains that the same angle in two charts with different totals stands for different numbers.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.LINE_GRAPH.mastery: The child plots the points and joins them in order, reads a rise or fall as the difference of two readings, finds the steepest rise, and reads a value halfway between two points on a straight part.

MATH.G7.DATA_H.DATA_HANDLING.TRAVEL_GRAP.mastery: On a distance-time graph the child reads a flat part as a stop, finds the speed of each part from its own distance and time, finds the average speed with the stop included (total distance / total time), and reads the time where two lines cross as when they meet.
